CNC machining a 29-inch display housing

A broad display housing with recessed faces, edge details and mounting features.

Study sections
The component
Machining setup
Machined features
Inspection planning

The photographs come from the LZZ workshop and show the part shapes and setups discussed here.

Photography & project scope
Discuss your drawing
01 · LZZ workshop
The component

This housing is identified in the workshop records as a 29-inch display enclosure. Broad rectangular panels carry slots and mounting features. The display size does not specify the enclosure dimensions; those must come from the drawing.

02 · LZZ workshop
Machining setup

The panel is supported across the machine table beneath the spindle. The machining photographs show the broad internal face and access from above. For a comparable enclosure, review support points, clamping areas, tool reach and the order of operations before choosing the setup.

Machined features

The panels have internal recesses, machined face patterns and narrow edge features. The paired view compares their two faces, while the workshop video provides a closer look at the overall form.

Inspection planning

For your enclosure, identify mounting datums, hole and slot positions, required flatness and mating-edge relationships. Specify cosmetic faces, finish and acceptance dimensions after treatment. Agree the measurement method and inspection records for the features that control assembly.

Two faces of the enclosure
Paired enclosure panels showing their internal and external faces.
Watch the display housing in the workshop

The clip shows a person holding and turning the machined panel, followed by a view of the CNC machine and workpiece. Compare the broad faces, internal recesses and overall form.
